# PR #4698: Patch: a job ran over 10 minutes

Closes #4690

## What changed and why

Shards `tools, wasm 1/4` (13m 43s) and `4/4` (14m 33s) were slow from skew, not uniform growth: two R4607000 fork-save tests from #4634 each replay whole deals and dominate their shards, while everything else in those shards sums to 2–3 minutes. A count cannot split one test, so per the plan I daily-moved the two monsters instead of raising the count:

- [fork_screen.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4690/crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs): `r4607000_resume_after_cut_prints_the_same_tally` and `r4607000_a_torn_last_line_is_played_again` are now `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` (super.yml's daily `tools` leg runs `-p jackioh-tools --tests -- --ignored`, so they still run daily). Each names its keeper, following the #4473 shape.
- Two new keepers plus a `hand_line` helper: `r4607000_a_hand_written_save_reprints_its_tally_without_playing` (finished file reprints with 0 probe calls; saved-path tally byte-equals the live `fork_tally` over the same lines, plus hand-computed `forks`/`forkEdge`/`rollouts` spot checks) and `r4607000_a_hand_written_torn_tail_is_dropped_and_reprinted` (torn tail dropped and healed with 0 games). Both run in 0.01 s.
- [ci-shards.toml](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4690/scripts/ci-shards.toml): `"tools, wasm"` comment refreshed with the measurements; count stays 4, so no person-side edit is needed anywhere.

No spec or ruling note: no rule, card, or engine behavior changes. Nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, or the pure crates touched.

## How I tested it

Timed all 10 deal-playing fork tests singly on this 2-CPU box (CI has 4 cores, so read relatively): resume_after_cut 810 s, torn 517 s, finished 130 s, identity 81/35 s, partial 59 s, refuse-header 45 s, self 41 s, cap keeper 19 s, differing_once 5 s. Commands run and seen: keepers pass (`cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --exact <both keepers>`, 0.01 s); dailies skip by default (2 ignored, 0 run); `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance daily` passes (ignore-form check); shard 1 and shard 4 subsets re-run exactly as CI runs them — all green, tools-binary walls 183 s and 261 s here; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` (still expands 1/4–4/4) all pass. Projected CI shards: remaining tests ≈3 min here plus compile, well under 8 minutes; PR CI confirms the real times.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- Daily-move over trimming: the remaining per-PR tests are already small, and the natural trim (forking later so rollout arms shorten) would tie the save tests to game lengths for little gain — rejected.
- Assembly-level keepers over live keepers: a live cut-resume inherently costs a full deal plus the oracle run, so the keepers pin the file→tally wiring and torn-tail heal with hand-written lines (`tally_from_lines` reads only wins, faults and order, so opaque duel/hash strings suffice), while `partial`, `finished`, the identity tests and header-refusal keep live save paths per PR.
- No test renamed, so shard hashes are stable; the two millisecond keepers both hashed into shard 4, which is harmless. Fallbacks B (count to 8) and C (compile split) did not trigger.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |

| 1 | build, 59.7 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 8s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 424s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 4s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 7s |

</details>

- [ ] The dominant test(s) hashing to shards 1/4 are identified with measured times recorded in the `scripts/ci-shards.toml` comment.
- [ ] The trim or daily-move plus keeper is in place; the touched test and keeper pass via `cargo test -p <crate> <name>`.

- [ ] Projected shard time (slowest shard's measured test seconds, scaled by the trim, plus its compile seconds) is under 8 minutes with headroom; CI on the pull request confirms the real times.
- [ ] If fallback B or C triggered instead, the count edit or the stop report is done and the exact person-side lines are in Open questions.

- Local timing is not CI timing (shared machine versus 4-core runners): mitigate by comparing relative dominance and compile-versus-test splits, not absolute seconds, and letting PR CI confirm.
- Trimming game/seed counts can weaken a statistical assertion or break the perf budgets last set in `af27372ba8`: keep the assertion's property identical at small size, and keep a daily full-size test wherever the property needs volume (the #4473 pattern).
- Renaming a test changes its shard hash and can move load between shards: after any rename, re-run step 1's shard listing and check no other shard inherits two heavy tests.
- Doc tests of the group run whole in shard 1 (`ci.yml` step `cargo test`, lines 436–438): if shard 1 alone stays slow after the fix, suspect `--doc` output before raising the count.

## Open questions

- None for the primary fix. If fallback B triggers: person, please update `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` `JOBS` (lines 28–34) replacing `"tools, wasm 1/4", "tools, wasm 2/4", "tools, wasm 3/4", "tools, wasm 4/4"` with `"tools, wasm 1/8"` through `"tools, wasm 8/8"`, and the `test_the_committed_files_give_todays_jobs` shard assertions accordingly.
